propositions: Current sidecar replacement mechanisms permit last-writer record loss and lack observational proof of durability across the write window
HLC and recent-create implementations have sibling-file locked read-modify-write patterns that should be generalized into a single reusable exclusive-path-lock primitive in fsutil
Sidecar persistence must calculate deltas against an immutable deep baseline, apply mutations under shared lock, and detect both upserts and deletions across concurrent writers
Concurrent distinct-key updates must retain all records while same-key updates follow last-lock-holder-wins semantics, proven by barrier-controlled tests
Lock acquisition, JSON validation, or atomic-write failures must log warnings, preserve target bytes, and allow reconciliation to continue fail-open without data corruption
